statement: On a die, opposite faces add up to 7. A die sits on a table showing 5 on top and 3 on the face towards you. What is the sum of the numbers on its left face and its right face?

choices.misconception: I found the bottom face 2 and the back face 4 and added those instead of the left and right faces.
I added the two numbers I was given, 5 and 3.
I took 21 and subtracted the top and front, which adds up the left, right, bottom and back faces together.
I thought I needed to know which number is on the left before I could find the sum.

hints: Where are the left and right faces compared with each other?
Left and right are opposite faces, just like top and bottom. Think about what the rule for opposite faces says, whichever numbers they turn out to be.
Left and right are a pair of opposite faces, and every pair of opposite faces has the same total.

solutions.reliable: The left face and the right face are opposite each other, and on this die every pair of opposite faces adds up to 7. So the left and right faces add to 7, even though we cannot tell which is which. (Top 5 with bottom 2, and front 3 with back 4, use up the other two pairs, so left and right are 1 and 6 in some order.) The transferable idea: notice when a question only needs a total, which can be fixed even when the separate values are not.

whyOnTest: The given numbers are a distraction, and the opposite-faces rule answers the question directly, a common shape for 3-point dice questions.
